summary: Iteration 6 testing of the labor time clock (backend endpoints + TimeClockPanel UI) and settings.labor_rate. Added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6.py (19 tests) — full suite now 81/81 pass (includes iterations 1-5 regression). Frontend flows verified end-to-end with Playwright: settings labor rate persistence, clock-in live timer, clock-out auto labor computation, log deletion recompute, PDF export. One CRITICAL frontend crash found and fixed (Settings page used t() without the useLang hook → whole /settings route threw a React error and rendered nothing).

minor.issue: Takes the full GarageSettings model, so any client that omits a field silently resets it to the model default (e.g. a partial PUT would wipe name/address or reset labor_rate to 45). Consider a partial/optional update model.

No concurrency guard — the running-log check is read-then-write, so two simultaneous clock-in requests could both insert a running log. Low risk for single-garage use; an atomic update filter would harden it.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: page called t("garageName") but never imported/used useLang → ReferenceError, entire /settings route crashed (blank page, no labor rate field). Added `import { useLang } from "@/i18n"` + `const { t } = useLang()`. Please review — the remaining labels on that page are still hardcoded English while the label uses i18n.

integration_issues.issue: repairLabels(t) in Repairs.jsx does not pass timeClock/startedAt/stopped/duration labels, so the PDF 'Labor time clock' block always falls back to hardcoded English headers even in NL/AR (RTL) mode.

Not reachable through the UI (the Clock in button is swapped for Clock out while a log runs), so the 400 toast path is only covered by backend tests. A second browser tab with stale state also correctly shows Clock out. No defect, informational.

design_issues.screen: Repair card editor — Labor time clock
issues: Log rows and the Duration tile round to whole minutes, so short sessions display '0m' while the € cost shows a non-zero value (e.g. 0m / 0,07 €) — consider showing seconds or 1 decimal for sub-minute logs.
PDF time-log duration is also rounded to whole minutes (0 min for short sessions).

action_items: Review the Settings.jsx useLang fix applied by the tester (or convert the remaining hardcoded English labels on that page to i18n).
Pass timeClock/startedAt/stopped/duration into repairLabels(t) so the PDF time-log table is translated.
Optional: make PUT /api/settings a partial update model; show sub-minute precision in the time log rows.
critical_code_review_comments: Settings.jsx referenced t() with no hook — this class of bug is caught instantly by loading each route once after edit; consider a smoke test over all routes.
clock-in/clock-out/manual/delete each duplicate the same 'recompute labor_charge from completed logs' block in server.py — extract a helper (_apply_time_logs) to keep the rate math in one place.
server.py is ~1700 lines; split into routers (repairs, inventory, invoices, settings).

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all time-clock flows pass; 1 crash found & fixed)

seed_data_creation: Created TEST_ repair cards via API and TEST_UI_* cards via UI — all deleted by cleanup_iter6.py (verified none remain). settings.labor_rate intentionally left at 60.0 (test suite sets it; no teardown restore to avoid xdist races).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration6.py covers labor_rate settings, clock-in/out, duplicate/no-running 400s, manual time logs (incl. bad ISO / stop<=start), delete-log recompute, manual labor override overwritten by clock-out, staff clocking, and card delete cleanup. NOTE: settings are global — test_iteration6 uses an autouse fixture that PUTs labor_rate=60 before each test and deliberately does NOT restore, because a teardown write races the second xdist worker (this caused one flaky 67.5 vs 90.0 failure before the change). The Settings page renders only because of the useLang fix in /app/frontend/src/pages/Settings.jsx.
rca_of_the_issue: Settings page: `<Label>{t("garageName")}</Label>` was added without importing the i18n hook, so `t` was an undefined identifier → ReferenceError during render → React unmounted the route (console: 'An error occurred in the <Settings> component'), making the new labor rate field unreachable. Fixed by adding useLang() to the component. Backend labor math verified correct: labor_charge = round(total_completed_minutes/60 * settings.labor_rate, 2) and grand_total = parts_total + labor_charge, persisted and re-read via GET.
